**6B.2 Research Note: Narendra Modi (2024)**

**Bottom line**
The evidence is **mixed, leaning positive on program reach but not on lived outcomes**. Modi’s 2024 government did push real access-expanding measures in health, housing, rural livelihoods, and social protection, and it kept spending relatively disciplined. But the record also shows that poor households still faced food inflation, rural distress, uneven education protection, and politically skewed distribution. I did **not** find equally strong direct evidence on water and sanitation outcomes in the material reviewed, so that part of the lens remains only partially evidenced.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Title:** Interim budget prioritized the poor, women, youth, and farmers  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 1 Feb 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that the budget explicitly centered disadvantaged groups while avoiding a giveaway structure. This is strong evidence that access to basic welfare was a stated governing priority rather than a purely rhetorical one.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1

- **Title:** Government resisted pre-election populism and kept fiscal consolidation  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 1 Feb 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/economy/india-refrains-from-populist-budget-before-election-trims-fiscal-deficit/1948823/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters said the government resisted election giveaways and stayed on a deficit-reduction path. That matters for welfare access because it suggests the state was still trying to preserve macro room for public services rather than blowing resources on short-term patronage.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 5B.10

- **Title:** Strong FY24 growth created fiscal space for public services  
  **Publisher:** Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation / PIB  
  **Date:** 31 May 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2022323&lang=2&reg=3  
  **Claim summary:** The government’s own release said real GDP grew 8.2% in FY 2023-24 and 7.8% in Q4. This does not prove better service access by itself, but it supports the claim that the administration had macro capacity to fund health, education, housing, and protection programs.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 5B.10

- **Title:** Expanded health coverage and digital health rollout in first 100 days  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
  **Date:** 28 Sep 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153215&lang=1&reg=3  
  **Claim summary:** The government highlighted expanded Ayushman Bharat coverage for seniors, U-WIN, new medical seats, and digital health registries. This is direct positive evidence for access to basic health services, though it is official self-reporting rather than independent outcome verification.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2

- **Title:** ABDM expanded large-scale digital health infrastructure  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare  
  **Date:** 17 Dec 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2085201&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The government said ABDM had built large-scale digital health infrastructure, including ABHA accounts and linked health records. This is positive evidence for more scalable access and continuity of care.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2

- **Title:** Digital Agriculture Mission aimed at farmer support and service delivery  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare  
  **Date:** 2 Sep 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2050966&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The mission used digital public infrastructure, crop estimation, and data-driven support for farmers. This is relevant to food security and rural welfare because it improves state targeting and support capacity for a large vulnerable population.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 5B.10

- **Title:** Rural women mobilized into self-help groups at very large scale  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development  
  **Date:** 30 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039162&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The ministry said DAY-NRLM had mobilized more than 10 crore women into self-help groups across states and UTs. That is strong evidence of expanded social protection and economic inclusion for poorer women.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2

- **Title:** Minority-women empowerment schemes continued  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Minority Affairs  
  **Date:** 11 Dec 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2083334&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The government said PM VIKAS/Nai Roshni trained about 4.35 lakh minority women with rights, literacy, and leadership content. This is useful welfare evidence, though it is official self-reporting.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1

- **Title:** Manipur relief package included food, medicine, and rehabilitation for displaced people  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Home Affairs  
  **Date:** 17 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2025980&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The Home Ministry said it was committed to safety for citizens in Manipur and outlined support for food, water, medicine, education, and rehabilitation. This is direct evidence of social-protection response, though it was reactive and crisis-driven.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 3B.1

- **Title:** PMAY-G and women’s asset ownership  
  **Publisher:** PTI via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 31 Dec 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/women-empowerment-remained-in-focus-for-rural-development-ministry-in-2024/2425889/  
  **Claim summary:** The rural development ministry said over half of MGNREGS beneficiaries were women and PMAY-G housing strongly favored women’s ownership. This is solid evidence for housing access and gender-targeted social protection.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2

- **Title:** PMAY-G expansion with differentiated support for hill and northeast states  
  **Publisher:** Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development  
  **Date:** 9 Aug 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2043919&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim summary:** The Cabinet extended PMAY-G with different unit assistance for hill and northeastern states. This is a genuine access measure because it adapts housing support to regional cost differences rather than treating everyone uniformly.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2

**Counterevidence**

- **Title:** Rural voters cited lack of jobs and high inflation  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 7 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/rural-vote-fall-cost-indias-modi-a-decisive-election-win/2121496/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that BJP losses in rural constituencies were driven by jobs and inflation problems. That is strong evidence that access to basic economic security had not translated into broad lived improvement for many rural households.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 5B.10

- **Title:** Survey reporting tied weaker support to prices, jobs, and falling incomes  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 6 Jun 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/modis-appeal-clouded-in-india-election-by-prices-jobs-graft-survey-says/2119215/  
  **Claim summary:** The reporting linked voter concern to prices, jobs, and falling incomes. This undercuts the claim that Modi’s welfare agenda had clearly improved daily access to basic necessities.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 5B.10

- **Title:** Food inflation squeezed school meal quality for poor children  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 11 Oct 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-high-food-inflation-leaves-less-in-lunch-boxes-of-poor-school-children/2307077/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters reported that school meal budgets had not kept pace with food inflation, forcing cutbacks in nutrition for poor children. This is direct counterevidence on food security and child welfare.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2

- **Title:** Manipur violence, displacement, and shutdowns persisted  
  **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  **Date:** 11 Jan 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/india-increased-abuses-against-minorities-critics  
  **Claim summary:** HRW reported deaths, displacement, destroyed homes/churches, and prolonged internet shutdowns in Manipur. That is strong evidence that access to basic protection and essential services was not reliably secured in at least one major crisis zone.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 3B.1

- **Title:** Amnesty said authorities failed to protect displaced residents in Manipur  
  **Publisher:** Amnesty International  
  **Date:** 16 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/india-authorities-missing-in-action-amid-ongoing-violence-and-impunity-in-manipur-state-new-testimonies/  
  **Claim summary:** Amnesty said the BJP-led state and central governments failed to end the violence, protect displaced residents, or hold vigilante groups accountable. This is direct counterevidence against a broad welfare-improvement claim.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 3B.1

- **Title:** HRW said repression persisted in Jammu and Kashmir  
  **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch  
  **Date:** 31 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/31/india-repression-persists-jammu-and-kashmir  
  **Claim summary:** HRW reported arbitrary detention, extrajudicial killings, and little accountability. That weakens any claim that the state broadly improved basic protection and social welfare for all groups.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 3B.1

- **Title:** Post-election budget spending was explicitly tied to vote-retention  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 23 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters said the budget devoted large sums to jobs, rural programs, and coalition states to win back voters and retain support. This is welfare spending, but it is also patronage and coalition bargaining, which weakens the claim that access improvements were purely need-based.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1

- **Title:** Opaque electoral finance favored the ruling party  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 16 Feb 2024  
  **URL:** https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/  
  **Claim summary:** Reuters described unlimited anonymous donations that heavily benefited the BJP. That is indirect but meaningful counterevidence because it points to capture-prone politics rather than cleanly universal provision of social goods.  
  **Question IDs:** 6B.2, 6B.1

**Synthesis**
- **Best positive case:** Modi’s government did expand or at least continue real access-oriented programs in health, housing, farmer support, and women-centered social protection.
- **Best negative case:** those gains sat alongside persistent rural distress, food inflation, coercive crisis management, and politically skewed distribution.
- **Overall:** I would rate this **mixed, leaning somewhat positive on programmatic access expansion, but not clearly positive on lived outcomes for all groups**.
- **Search gap:** I found strong material on health, housing, rural women, and food-related stress, but **much weaker direct evidence on water and sanitation outcomes** in the available set.
